reason: Scratch lifetime is a small, source-expressible change with low arithmetic risk, though its expected gain is limited and unmeasured. Transpose fusion targets A conversion directly and could remove scratch traffic, but repeats A loads across 16 column panels and has high implementation and correctness risk. The counter-width change is narrow and preserves arithmetic order; prior loop-schedule results show no reliable gain, not evidence about this distinct change. ZA issue reordering is feasible but may change rounding, with no evidence of accumulator reuse benefit. Per-panel B packing adds timed work and requires coordinated traversal changes; the measured full-B packing variant regressed, though it tested a different layout. The last two IDs propose the same N=64 helper approach, which is unavailable in the supplied source; treat them as tied and abstain unless a host-validated helper is provided. No proposal has measured evidence of exceeding 1800 GFLOP/s.
